title: Model Fit Tagging Taxonomy & Rapid Recon Runbook
creator: Nadia Morales
description: Create a repeatable taxonomy and lightweight reconnaissance playbook for rapidly assessing third-party and open models for regional/vertical fit. Deliverables include a tag schema, a short checklist used by SEs and AE scouts, an automated dashboard spec, and a prioritized backlog of candidate models for integration experiments. This ticket coordinates PM research, a one-week pilot with two SEs, and follow-up handoff to onboarding and runtime engineering.
background: We often discover model variants that look promising in raw benchmarks but fail in downstream enterprise prompts because of subtle regional behaviors (date formats, safety heuristics, formal tone). Sales and Solutions Engineering teams need a fast, consistent way to evaluate 'fit' across legal, latency, cost, and prompt-quality axes. Existing playbooks are ad-hoc and live in individual notes; this effort centralizes guidance and produces tags that feed the watchlist pipeline.
goals: Define a concise model-fit tag taxonomy (<= 12 tags) that maps to product decisions (serveable, needs quantization, region-only, unsafe)
Ship a 1-page SE/AE reconnaissance checklist for <30 minute evals
Prototype an import pipeline that converts tag annotations into watchlist signals
Prioritize top 15 candidate models for 1-week integration experiments
scope: Pilot recon checklist and training session
Automation spec for converting tags to watchlist entries
Handoff artifacts for ENG and Onboarding teams
out_of_scope: Full model onboarding (weight transfers, infra tuning)
deliverables: pilot-report-15-models.csv with tags and qualitative notes
stakeholders: Priya Sharma (Research) - sample prompts and eval harness
metrics: Time to first-pass tag per model <= 45 minutes
Tag inter-rater agreement (Cohen's Kappa) >= 0.6 across 3 SEs
% of pilot models with clear serveability recommendation >= 60%
Number of watchlist signals generated per week (target 5-10)
research_tasks: Collect 20 candidate models across open and hosted providers (Priya)
Assemble 10 representative enterprise prompts per vertical (Sales)
Run prompt-level failure modes and annotate with draft taxonomy (SE pilot)
Survey competitor documentation for regional opt-out/locale-specific behaviors
decisions: Keep taxonomy intentionally small (<=12 tags) to reduce cognitive load
Use 'serveability' as a required top-level tag: serveable / conditional / blocked
Map four operational dimensions to tags: latency, cost, safety, locale-behavior
Pilot will focus on EMEA and US variants; APAC follow-up in next cycle
tradeoffs: Granularity vs speed: finer tags give better fidelity but slow scouting; we favor speed for discovery
Automated signals vs human judgment: automation will bootstrap the watchlist but human review required for legal/safety-sensitive tags
Surface-area vs adoption: fewer tags increases adoption across SEs but may lose nuance for runtime decisions
notes: Leila reported a consistent 'formal tone' failure on three models for French customer-facing prompts
Priya suggests adding a small set of localized evaluation prompts (dates, addresses, currency) to the harness
Claire: any tag implying 'unsafe' requires a one-paragraph rationale and quick legal triage checklist
